newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian markets rally on Yeltsin operation news.
newsitem.headline: Russian markets rally on Yeltsin operation news.

text.p: Russian markets rallied on Wednesday on news that doctors believe President Boris Yeltsin will be able to undergo a successful heart operation after another six to eight weeks of preparation.

Russian cardiologist Renat Akchurin, who is likely to conduct the operation said after Russian and foreign doctors had met Yeltsin that the delay in the operation should increase the president's chances of survival to 100 percent.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares rose 1.62 percent to 159.70 on heavy volume of $25.70 million.
"The market reacted positively," said Anton Kudryashov, head of equity trading at Renaissance-Capital. "There is certainty at last that the operation will take place."
He said he expected the trend to continue to at least the end of the week.

Russia's biggest oil company LUKoil rose to $8.95 from $8.72 at Tuesday's close, Moscow electricity utility Mosenergo was $0.859 after $0.832 and national power company UES rose to $0.0738 from $0.0716.

Prices fell sharply at the beginning of the week on investors' worries that Yeltsin was too weak to undergo an operation after Akchurin said on Sunday that the operation might be delayed or called off altogether.
But Oleg Martynenko, chief trader at Bank Rossiisky Kredit, warned the delay meant several more weeks of uncertainty.
"Foreign clients do not like uncertainty, that's why I think that there will be no global growth and the market will soon fall again," he said.
Prices of dollar-denominated MinFin bonds, which are actively traded in Russia and abroad, rose on the news too.

"Buying resumed when it was said the operation will take place. It is a positive factor as it is at least some official information and the operation is expected to be successful," said an International Moscow Bank dealer.
But yields of Treasury bills rose sharply at two auctions on Wednesday and dealers said one reason was that foreign investors had stayed away because of worries about Yeltsin's health.
Bids for the auctions were made on Tuesday.

An issue of six-month T-bills yielded an average 82.62 percent after 61.25 percent at the previous auction last week. The yield on an issue of three-month T-bill rose to 69.12 percent from 65.77 percent at the previous auction.

The main reason for the rise in yields was heavy sales of paper by the authorities in the secondary market earlier this week, making it clear to investors that the finance ministry was in desperate need of cash to pay striking workers.
The rouble ignored the news and remained steady as banks sought funds to square their books and meet compulsory reserve requirements of the central bank for the quarter-end.
Tomorrow roubles edged up to 5,397-99 from yesterday's late 5,399-5,401. Overnight credits yielded 60-80 percent compared with Tuesday's late 5-10 percent.
